name: Let's Verify Step by Step
problem: Even state-of-the-art models regularly produce logical mistakes, and it is unclear which of two supervision regimes - OUTCOME supervision (feedback on the final result only) or PROCESS supervision (feedback on each intermediate step) - is better and more cost-effective to collect.
mechanism: Compares the two regimes directly. Process supervision labels each intermediate reasoning step as correct or not, enabling a PROCESS REWARD MODEL. Findings: process supervision significantly outperforms outcome supervision on the MATH dataset, and ACTIVE LEARNING (having the model itself flag its own uncertain steps for human labelling) markedly improves process-supervision efficiency, which matters because human feedback is the expensive input. Releases PRM800K, 800,000 step-level human feedback labels.
speedup_reported: Process-supervised model solves 78% of problems from a representative subset of the MATH test set. Active learning significantly improves the efficacy of process supervision - i.e. it raises the LABEL-YIELD per unit of human effort, which is the cost number that matters, since human feedback is the bottleneck rather than GPU time.
notes: ADOPTION: the PROCESS REWARD MODEL idea is in production - step-level verification is used in deployed reasoning systems (best-of-N over process-rewarded samples is one of the cheapest accuracy gains available), and PRM800K is a released dataset, so open_weights is recorded as true for the model/dataset artifacts rather than for a single checkpoint. VENUE NOTE: no peer-reviewed venue verifiable via Semantic Scholar; the arXiv comment carries no venue, so venue = arxiv-preprint, year = ArXiv v1 (May 2023). TIES THE TWO HALVES OF THIS SUB-AREA TOGETHER, which is why it is included in the inference-time-compute slice rather than the training slice: a PRM is what makes SAMPLED reasoning (self-consistency, best-of-N) pay off, and it is the EXTERNAL FEEDBACK that pap-eff-llms-cannot-self-correct-reasoning shows is missing in the intrinsic case. A step-level verifier costs an extra forward pass per step, so it is a real serving cost that belongs on the same accounting sheet as the reasoning tokens it screens.
